title: Copy Frameworks
description: Write outreach emails that get responses using campaign-tested copy frameworks, including SPARK, PAS, AIDA, and a follow-up Nudge

children.text: Write emails that get responses using proven copy frameworks. Given a goal and audience, pick the right framework, apply it, and produce two ready-to-send variants.

### SPARK (recommended for cold or warm outreach)
- **S**ituation: establish context quickly
- **P**roblem: name the pain or gap
- **A**ngle: your unique take or hook
- **R**elevance: why this matters to them specifically
- **K**ick: clear, low-friction CTA

### PAS (Problem-Agitate-Solution)
Best for: re-engagement when the pain is well understood.
Name the problem, amplify why it matters, offer the solution.

### AIDA (Attention-Interest-Desire-Action)
Best for: introducing something new.
Hook attention, build interest, create desire, drive action.

### The Nudge
Best for: following up on silence.
Acknowledge the non-reply, restate value in one sentence, make an even easier ask.

Based on the user's goal:
- First contact or warm lead? Use SPARK.
- Following up on silence? Use the Nudge.
- Re-engaging someone who said "later"? Use PAS.
- Introducing a new offer? Use AIDA.

Apply the chosen framework. Rules:
- Subject line: specific, not clever. Under 8 words.
- Opening line: no "I hope this finds you well." Start with them, not you.
- Body: 3-5 sentences max.
- CTA: one ask, low friction. "Does this still make sense?" beats "Schedule a call."
- No attachments on first touch.

Produce 2 variants using different frameworks so there is a choice. Label each.

```
## Variant 1, [Framework Name]
Subject: [subject]

[email body]

---

## Variant 2, [Framework Name]
Subject: [subject]

[email body]
```
